text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Suryasiddhanta: Siddhantic mean-planet system with Rsine-table epicycles
formula: Ch.1 Madhyamadhikara (mean planets, time units), Ch.2 Spashtadhikara (true planets). The Hindi commentary adds derivations and a worked example for Vikrama 1978 (1921 CE) that the engine reproduces.
notes: Read by page image from the scan. Numerals were read from the printed Devanagari figures (Arabic numerals appear in the Hindi translation); Numerals were later checked against the Sanskrit text of the Pandey/Chaukhamba edition (see SS.concordance); the Devanagari verses themselves are not stored in the registry. Chapters 3-14 (time, direction, place, eclipses, conjunctions, star table, heliacal rising, Bhugola, measures) are located but not yet interpreted for this release; only the ayanamsa rule (3.9-12) is already in the engine as treatise model SuryaNilakantha (AY rules).

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Revolutions and civil days in a mahayuga (4,320,000 years)
formula: Sun, Mercury sighra, Venus sighra counted with the Sun 4,320,000; Moon 57,753,336; Mars 2,296,832; Mercury sighra 17,937,060; Jupiter 364,220; Venus sighra 7,022,376; Saturn 146,568; Moon apogee 488,203; Moon node -232,238 (retrograde). Civil days 1,577,917,828; lunar months 53,433,336; adhimasas 1,593,336; ksaya tithis 25,082,252
notes: Printed numerals checked on page 18 and 30-31 of the book (PDF 41, 53-54). Sidereal year implied: 365.258756 days. The Source Book compares other siddhantas: Brahmagupta 1,577,916,450; Aryabhatiya 1,577,917,500; Pancasiddhantika Surya 1,577,917,800.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Mean longitudes from the Kali epoch
formula: longitude = 360*frac(D*rev/civil_days). All planets are at 0 (Mesa start) at the beginning of Kali (half a mahayuga after the end of Krta); apogee of the Moon is at 90 deg (Karka) and its node at 180 deg (Tula) at that epoch. D = days from Kali midnight at Ujjayini (JD 588465.5), measured continuously
notes: Moon apogee at Karka start follows from 488,203*0.75 mahayuga = .25 rev, node -232,238*0.75 = .5 rev (from the end of Krta). The commentator also quotes Bhaskara's different Kali-epoch values for the Moon apogee and node. Worked example check (Vikrama 1978, D = 1,834,977): Jupiter mean 6s19d52'37'' (book 6s19d52'37'', exact); Mercury sighra 2s9d29'17'' (book 2s9d29'17'').

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
reference: Ch.1 vv.41-47; commentary example in Ch.2
title: Manda apsides (mandocca) and nodes of the planets
formula: Per kalpa revolutions: Sun 387, Mars 204, Mercury 368, Jupiter 900, Venus 535, Saturn 39 (mandocca, eastward); nodes Mars 214, Mercury 488, Jupiter 174, Venus 903, Saturn 662 (westward). Position = 360*frac(rev*Y/4.32e9) with Y = Sun-years since creation = 1,955,880,000 at the start of Kali + elapsed years
notes: Verified to 0.1 arc-second against the book's worked example (Y = 1,955,885,023): Sun 2s17d17'31.17'', Mercury 7s10d28'26.54'', Jupiter 5s21d22'36.21''. The same method gives Mars 4s10d02'43'', Venus 2s19d52'26'', Saturn 7s26d37'35''. Today's Sun apogee is about 77.3 deg. These apsides move so slowly that over a few centuries they are effectively fixed.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Rsine table (24 steps of 3 deg 45 min, R = 3438)
formula: Differences 225,224,222,219,215,210,205,199,191,183,174,164,154,143,131,119,106,93,79,65,51,37,22,7. Sine of an intermediate angle by linear interpolation (v.31-32); arc from a given sine by the inverse rule (v.33)
notes: Entries confirmed in the commentary: 17th = 3084, 18th = 3177 (p.129). Cumulative sum = 3438. Same 24 values as the 'AR/SS' column of the Tantrasangraha table. The linear interpolation is the text's own rule; `exact=True` replaces it with math.sin to show how much the rule matters (under 0.1 arc-minute in the phala).

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Manda and sighra epicycle circumferences (degrees of 360)
formula: Manda at ends of even padas (anomaly 0, 180) / odd padas (90, 270): Sun 14 / 13d40'; Moon 32 / 31d40'; Mars 75 / 72; Mercury 30 / 28; Jupiter 33 / 32; Venus 12 / 11; Saturn 49 / 48. Sighra: Mars 235 / 232; Mercury 133 / 132; Jupiter 70 / 72; Venus 262 / 260; Saturn 39 / 40. Corrected circumference = even value + (odd - even)*|Rsin(anomaly)|/R
notes: Saturn sighra at even padas is printed 36 in the Vijnana-bhashya Hindi translation (page 131) but 39 in the Sanskrit verse 2.36 ('go-naya' = 9,3) and in Pandey's edition (p.70, 39); 39 used. The 36 is a misprint of the Hindi edition. Mars manda even-end printed 75 and sighra 235 as expected. The commentator quotes the Sun's maximum equation as 2d13'41'' (p.132), which is the arc of 14*3438/360 = 133.7'; with the corrected circumference 13d40' at anomaly 90 the engine gives 2d10'.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Manda equation (bhujaphala and arc)
formula: bhujaphala = circumference * Rsin(anomaly) / 360 (in the 3438 radius); manda phala = arc whose Rsine is bhujaphala. With anomaly a = mean - apogee: true = mean - phala
notes: The commentary derives the formula from the epicycle geometry (figs. 30, 31) and says the exact karna correction is neglected for manda.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Sighra equation (karna and arc)
formula: kotiphala = circumference * Rcos(anomaly)/360 added to R if the anomaly is in Makara..Mithuna (270..90), subtracted if in Karka..Dhanus; karna = sqrt((R +- kotiphala)^2 + bhujaphala^2); phala = arc of Rsine R*bhujaphala/karna. true = planet + phala
notes: Same triangle rule as Aryabhata/TS, with epicycles that vary with the anomaly.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Four corrections for Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn
formula: 1) half the sighra phala to the mean planet, 2) half the manda phala of that (anomaly from the apogee), 3) full manda phala (recomputed from the result) to the mean, 4) full sighra phala (anomaly from the manda-corrected planet). For Mercury and Venus the 'mean planet' is the mean Sun and the sighrocca the planet's own sighra mean; for the other three the sighrocca is the mean Sun
notes: Order is identical to TS 2.26 and DG.4step.exterior. Applied to the worked example (Jupiter) the engine reproduces every intermediate value: first sighra phala 636' (book; engine 639' with true arcs), half-corrected manda anomaly 10s26d12', first manda phala 172', second 166', second sighra anomaly 81d6', second sighra phala 647' (engine 650'), final 6s27d53'37'' (engine 6s27d53'24'' when the commentator's shortcut is used, 6s27d56'57'' with true arcs).

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: True Sun and Moon: one manda correction
formula: true = mean - manda phala(mean - apogee); Sun apogee from the apsides table; Moon apogee is its own mean apogee
notes: Worked example: true Sun at Vikrama 1978 Vasanta-pancami midnight = mean 9s8d12'6'' + 47' = 9s8d59'6'' (book; engine 9s8d59'25''). The Hindi text prints the sign index of the Sun as 6; the arithmetic (mean Sun 9s8d) shows the sign as 9.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Retrograde motion by the sighra anomaly
formula: Retrograde from final sighra anomaly 164 (Mars), 144 (Mercury), 130 (Jupiter), 163 (Venus), 115 (Saturn) degrees; direct again at 360 minus these (196, 216, 230, 197, 245). v.55: because the sighra epicycle is large, the retrograde motion ends (the planet is again direct) when the anomaly is in the 7th sign for Mars and Venus, the 8th for Mercury and Jupiter, the 9th for Saturn, which matches the end values 196/197, 216, 230, 245
notes: Tested on 2022-23 retrogrades (Mars Dec 2022, Jupiter Oct 2022, Saturn Sep 2023) with SS errors of several degrees allowed. Printed numeral for the end of Venus' retrograde is read 197 (=360-163).

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Daily true motion (spashta gati) and retrograde speed
formula: Sun/Moon/planets: mean daily motion corrected by manda and sighra gati phala (equation 4 in the commentary), with the formula R-karna and vakra gati
notes: Not implemented: only longitudes are needed for the experiments. Worked example (Sun 61'16'', Jupiter 7'8'' per day) is printed on pp.159-160.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: Worked example: Vikrama 1978 Vasanta-pancami midnight (1921 CE), Sun, Mercury, Jupiter
formula: Ahargana 1,834,977 days; creation years 1,955,885,023; mean Sun 9s8d12'6''; mean Jupiter 6s19d52'37''; Mercury sighra 2s9d29'17''; apsides as in SS.apsides; true Sun 9s8d59'6''; true Jupiter 6s27d53'37''
notes: The commentator rounds to the minute and uses Rsine-as-arc for small phalas ('svalpantara'); the engine reproduces the example to 13-20 arc-seconds in that mode, and to 3.3 arc-minutes (Jupiter) if the verse's inverse-Rsine rule is applied literally. Both modes are selectable (`exact='book'` versus default).

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
title: How the SS sky compares with the modern sky
formula: SS mean Sun meets the tropical mean Sun in AD 516 (the SS sidereal year is 3.45 min too long, drift -0.24 deg/century). Relative to the SS Sun the Moon has no drift (rms 1.5 deg); Mars -0.26, Jupiter +0.58, Saturn -0.89 deg/century with zero errors near AD 1464, 1165, 1357. Venus is correct only near AD 800 and its error grows to a 6 deg rms by 1900-2025.
notes: See validation/validation_ss_2026-10.txt. In 1850-2025 the SS Jupiter is +4.5 deg and Saturn -5.1 deg off even after removing the Sun's frame error; TS is within 0.3 deg.

text: Suryasiddhanta (Hindi Vijnana-bhashya edition, Pt. Mahavir Prasad Srivastava; PDF 838 pp.)
reference: Sanskrit text of the R.C. Pandey / Chaukhamba edition (with Ranganatha's Gudharthaprakasha and Hindi translation, 387 pp.) against the Vijnana-bhashya edition
title: Edition comparison: Sanskrit verses versus the Hindi-commentary edition
formula: Checked verse by verse against the Sanskrit (numerals decoded from the bhuta-sankhya words): 1.28-33 revolutions; 1.34-39 civil days, lunar days, adhimasas, ksaya tithis, solar months; 1.41-44 apsis and node revolutions; 1.45-47 years to the end of Krta (1,953,720,000); 1.57-58 epoch positions; 2.17-27 Rsine table (all 24 values); 2.28 greatest declination Rsine 1397; 2.34-37 epicycles; 2.38 corrected circumference; 2.39-42 manda and sighra phala; 2.43-44 four corrections; 2.52-55 retrograde limits. All values agree with the engine with the exceptions below
notes: Exceptions: (1) Saturn even-pada sighra epicycle: Sanskrit and Pandey 39; Vijnana-bhashya Hindi translation prints 36 (misprint). (2) Kshepaka table (Pandey p.36, v.58, apsides and nodes at the end of Krta): Sun 0s7d28'12'', Mars 3s3d14'24'', Mercury 5s4d4'48'', Jupiter 0s9d0'0'', Venus 11s13d21'0'' all equal the engine's apsis formula; Saturn is printed 4s20d13'12'' (identical to the Saturn node entry, a printing duplicate); the engine formula gives 7s19d35'24''. (3) The kshepaka node values (Mars 9s11d20'12'', Mercury 8s11d16'48'', Jupiter 8s8d56'24'', Venus 4s17d25'48'', Saturn 4s20d13'12'') are the 360-degree complements of the engine's physical retrograde positions, so the book lists the forward revolution remainder to be subtracted; all five agree to 12''. (4) Pandey's text has v.57-58 'at the end of Krta all planets are at Mesa except the apsides and nodes: Moon apogee at Makara, node at Tula'; the engine's 90 deg (Karka) for the Moon apogee at Kali start is that value advanced half a mahayuga (488,203/2 revolutions, a half revolution). (5) Verse 2.44 and Ranganatha confirm the four-step order used by SS.4step: sighra, manda, manda, sighra, with half phalas in the middle steps. Ranganatha's commentary was not read in full; only the numerals and verses above were compared.
